title: Computing a unit-weighted selling price
scenario_markdown: A subscription retailer sells 100 basic packages at $10, 50 standard packages at $20, and 50 premium packages at $40. Find total revenue per package across all 200 packages, treating units sold as the weights.
assumptions: Prices and quantities refer to the same period and exclude tax and returns.
The target is revenue per package, so weights are unit counts rather than revenue shares.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the average selling price in dollars per package? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: The three products have unequal unit counts; do not weight them equally.
Revenue must be divided by the total number of packages.

stages.explanation_markdown: $\bar p_w=(10(100)+20(50)+40(50))/(100+50+50)=4000/200=20$. Excel: `=SUMPRODUCT(A2:A4,B2:B4)/SUM(B2:B4)` with prices in A and quantities in B.

stages.prompt_markdown: Why does the unweighted average of the three listed prices answer a different question?

options.text_markdown: It gives each product one vote instead of giving each sold package one vote.
An unweighted mean is always mathematically undefined when values differ.
options.hint_markdown: The arithmetic mean exists; its weights describe the wrong target here.

options.text_markdown: The highest price must receive the largest weight.
options.hint_markdown: Unit volume, not price, determines the weights for revenue per package.

stages.explanation_markdown: The unweighted price mean is $70/3=23.3333$. It describes an equally weighted product list. The transaction mix has twice as many basic packages as either other package, yielding $20 per package.
